VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed answer max{0, d−6} is not supported, and the solution contradicts itself. It says the curve is not linearly normal, which under the standard convention gives index −1 for every d, yet it still returns a d-dependent formula. The value at d = 5 is also doubtful. The projection C_q ⊂ P³ has degree 5 and genus 1. Quadrics in P³ containing C_q would be quadrics in P⁴ containing C that are singular at q. Generically the five quadrics through the elliptic normal quintic do not admit such a singular member, so C_q lies on no quadric. That makes the claimed index of 0 at d = 5 hard to justify.

I could not identify the source result for the general projection from P^{d−1} to P^{d−2} that fixes the intended formula. The answer should be checked against that result, most likely a Green–Lazarsfeld / Green K_{p,1}-type bound for projections of elliptic normal curves, and the proposed formula does not match what I can verify.

CONFIDENCE: 2
